commit_message:
[maglev] Introduce MapInference

This CL introduces `MapInference`, similar to TurboFan, to manage map
knowledge in Maglev.  Instead of clearing possible maps on side effects,
we now mark them as stale. This allows us to either ignore them or
re-verify them using `CheckMaps`.

All previous users of NodeInfo::possible_maps were updated to use the
MapInference interface; in addition to fetching the set of possible
maps, they are now required to call InsertMapChecks once the decision
has been made to use possible_maps.

InsertMapChecks only emits map checks when needed, ie when at least one
stale unstable map exists. Unreliable maps are "stale" when a side
effect may have occurred after we've last recorded them.

The --maglev-use-unreliable-maps flag, on by default, currently controls
whether Maglev uses stale unreliable maps by default, ie when no
explicit variant is passed to MapInference methods. Note that there is
no guarantee that *not* enabling this flag is identical to previous
behavior, since map tracking changed underneath (it should be similar
though). This flag is likely to be removed soon.

This CL also introduces KNA tracing: --trace-maglev-kna.

findings.title: TryInferApiHolderValue swallows abort signal from InsertMapChecks, causing use of dangling current_block_
findings.message: TryInferApiHolderValue() returns a plain compiler::HolderLookupResult. When inference.InsertMapChecks(zone()) detects that graph building has aborted (e.g. because a required map check could not be safely inserted and the current basic block was terminated/nulled), the function collapses this distinct 'abort' condition into the same 'not_found' sentinel value that it also returns for the ordinary, non-abort 'holder could not be inferred' case. The caller, MaglevGraphBuilder::TryBuildCallKnownApiFunction, cannot distinguish these two cases: it simply assigns the return value to api_holder and continues normal control flow via the switch on api_holder.lookup, falling through to emit further graph nodes (a CallBuiltin) into what is actually a dead/aborted block. AttachExceptionHandlerInfo (and other downstream code that assumes current_block_ is valid) then dereferences the now-null/invalid current_block_, causing a crash. This was introduced when MapInference was added and InsertMapChecks (which can internally abort graph building) was called with its abort result discarded/mapped to the ordinary not-found path.
findings.suggestion: Change TryInferApiHolderValue's return type to std::optional<compiler::HolderLookupResult> (or otherwise separately signal the abort condition) so that when InsertMapChecks aborts, the function returns std::nullopt instead of the same sentinel used for ordinary 'not found'. The caller (TryBuildCallKnownApiFunction) must check for this and immediately propagate ReduceResult::DoneWithAbort() instead of falling through to build further nodes in the now-dead block.

ground_truth.root_cause: Conflating two semantically distinct outcomes ('holder not found' vs 'graph building aborted') into a single sentinel return value, so the caller cannot detect that the compiler has entered a dead/aborted state and must stop emitting nodes.

must_cover.reason: Primary location of finding: TryInferApiHolderValue swallows abort signal from InsertMapChecks, causing use of dangling current_block_
